entries.text: Fuselage. This is the body of the airplane. People and bags travel inside.
Cockpit. The pilots sit here. They use the controls to fly the airplane.
Wings. Air flows around the wings. The wings make lift to help the airplane stay in the air.
Engines. The engines push air backward. This gives the airplane a push forward.
Landing gear. These wheels help the airplane roll on the ground. They support it when it lands.
Vertical tail. This tall tail helps the airplane stay steady. It helps keep the nose pointing forward.
Horizontal tail. These small tail wings help keep the airplane steady, so its nose does not tip too much.
Ailerons. These parts move on the wings. They help the airplane roll, with one wing up and one wing down.
Elevators. These parts move on the small tail wings. They help the airplane point its nose up or down.
Rudder. This part moves on the tall tail. It helps the airplane point its nose left or right.
Inlet. Air enters the engine here.
Fan. The fan moves air toward the back.
Bypass duct. This air travels around the engine core.
Compressor. The compressor squeezes the air.
Combustor. Fuel mixes with air and burns here.
Turbine. Hot gas turns the turbine.
Shaft. The shaft connects turning parts.
Nozzle. Gas leaves the engine at the back.
Body frames. These frames help hold the body in shape.
Cabin floor. The floor supports people and seats.
Passenger seats. Passengers sit in these seats.
Cargo hold. Bags travel below the cabin floor.
Pilot seats. The pilots sit at the front.
Instrument panel. These displays show how the airplane is flying.
Flight controls. Pilots use controls to guide the airplane.
Wing spar. A strong beam runs along the wing.
Wing ribs. These ribs help shape the wing.
Flap. Flaps help the wings make lift at low speeds.
Slat. Slats help the wings make lift at low speeds.
Spoiler. These panels rise to reduce lift.
Landing gear strut. The strut supports the airplane on the ground.
Wheel and tire. The wheels let the airplane roll.
Wheel brake. Brakes help slow the wheels down.
Landing gear bay. The wheels tuck into a space inside the airplane.
Tail frame. Spars and ribs support the upright tail.
Tailplane spar. A spar supports each horizontal tailplane.
Aileron hinge. Ailerons turn around hinges at the wing edge.
Control linkage. A short linkage moves the aileron.
Elevator hinge. Elevators turn together on the tail.
Rudder hinge. The rudder swings left and right.
